rules.title: Prohibition on sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or occupancy levels
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use a coordinated pricing algorithm (one that uses nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old) to set rents or occupancy levels for Berkeley residential units. Vendors may not sell, license, or provide such algorithms to Berkeley landlords.
rules.key_value: Ban; civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation (each month and each unit a separate violation)
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley, and anyone selling, licensing, or providing coordinated pricing algorithms to Berkeley landlords.
rules.exemptions: Products that publish aggregated, anonymous rental data without recommending rents or terms; products used to set rent or income limits under government affordable housing guidelines; information used for market research for project financing, appraisals, or software research, testing, or training (if competitor data is not an input when a recommendation is calculated).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only if the landlord uses a coordinated pricing algorithm relying on nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old.

rules.penalty: City Attorney may sue for damages, injunctive relief, restitution, and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; aggrieved tenants may sue for injunctive relief, damages, and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; prevailing City Attorney or tenant awarded attorney's fees and costs. Each month and each unit is a separate violation.
rules.citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.63 (§§ 13.63.030, 13.63.040), as amended by Ord. No. 7,992-N.S.
rules.quoted_span:
B. It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.
